FortiAnalyzer workspace

The FortiAnalyzer ADOM draws the unit's own GUI pages from the layout measured on its build, reads them live over JSON-RPC, writes only /cli/global configuration objects (dry run first, read back and verified), and links monitor and device-managed pages to the unit.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsnetwork.view network.edit network.apply protection.view users.manage audit.view registry.view
📍 WhereProduct selector → FortiAnalyzer (URL /faz/); measured pages at /workspace/<id>/fwgui/<page>; curated section pages at /faz/m/<item>

What is it?#

The FortiAnalyzer workspace is the SATOM ADOM for FortiAnalyzer log analytics units. When SATOM has GUI layouts for the selected unit's build (FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7 build 3737 is measured), the sidebar draws the unit's own menu and every page follows the measured device layout, read live over JSON-RPC. Configuration objects under /cli/global can be changed with a dry run first; monitors and pages the device manages through its own GUI calls are shown read-only and link to the unit. Without a layout, the curated section pages described below take their place.

What does it do?#

  • The FortiAnalyzer menu in the sidebar (when the unit's build has layouts): All pages and the pages of the unit's own GUI in its menu order — FortiView, Log View, Fabric View, Incidents & Events, Reports, System Settings and the others — followed by the Not in GUI, but in CLI group and the per-device Not in GUI, but in CLI page. On 7.6.7 build 3737 SATOM has 138 measured pages:
Kind of page What SATOM does
Configuration pages (Administrators, Admin Profiles, Network, Mail Server, Syslog Server...) Reads the /cli/global/... URL the layout names, live. Tables list their rows; a single object is one form. Create New, edit and Delete go to the object's own URL.
Not in GUI, but in CLI (43 pages, one per CLI object the GUI never edits, for example system ha, system ntp, fmupdate service) Same as a configuration page: drawn from the object's schema, read live, writable.
Monitors (FortiView, Log View, Event Monitor, Incidents, dashboards, Generated Reports...) Says Live monitor: <device> draws this page from live data (it is not configuration). with Open it on the device. SATOM queries nothing for it.
Pages the GUI edits through its own private calls (Event Handlers, Data Selectors, Notification Profiles, Report Definitions, Log Forwarding, ADOMs...) and GUI pages with no API (Device Manager, Task Monitor, HA) Drawn from the measured layout, read-only, with no Create New: Managed on the device: <device> edits this page through its own GUI calls, which SATOM never replays. SATOM draws its layout read-only; nothing is sent from it. and Open it on the device.
  • Writes go only to configuration objects under /cli/global/system/... and /cli/global/fmupdate/.... Every save is a dry run first that shows the exact JSON-RPC request; Apply reads the object, sends add, update or delete on the object's own URL, is audited and reads the object back to verify it. A table inside a row of another table, ADOM data (such as Meta Fields), monitors and device actions (the configuration backup) are never written. Passwords are never shown or sent back.
  • Dashboard (/faz/) — device picker plus an overview card per menu group with links to every section.
  • Section pages (/faz/m/<item>) — one page per curated menu leaf. Its tabs are the registry endpoints bound to that leaf; each tab is one live JSON-RPC read, so only the tab you open is fetched. They are the sidebar when the unit's build has no layout. When it has one, a section whose every tab a measured page draws redirects to that page (the requested tab's page, else the first) — on 7.6.7 build 3737, 12 of the 34 sections, for example Network, Admin, Certificates, Mail Server, Syslog Server and Log Forwarding. Sections with a monitor, ADOM-data, status or backup tab (Logs, Reports, Incidents, Devices & Groups, High Availability, Miscellaneous Settings...) or no tab keep their page; adding ?classic=1 to the URL always opens the section page.
  • Two layouts — a single configuration object is shown as a Setting / Value card; a list is shown as a table (up to eight columns, first 500 rows).
  • Editing — on configuration tables, Create New, a pencil per row (Edit) and a trash button per row (Delete); on single objects an Edit button. Every change is previewed first.
  • Device Manager actions — Authorize and Delete for log devices, plus display tools. See FortiAnalyzer Device Manager.
  • Panes without an API — sections whose GUI feature has no JSON-RPC list (for example Log Groups, Event Handlers, FortiAI Assistant) say <section> lives in the FortiAnalyzer console and offer Open in FortiAnalyzer and API & Registry.
  • Menu visibility — administrators can take the live-monitor and device-managed pages out of the menus under Settings → User Interface → ADOM Menus (see ADOM Menus). The curated menu has no hiding of its own.

Curated menu groups and sections#

The sidebar when the unit's build has no GUI layout, and the /faz/m/ section pages:

Group Sections (tabs)
Device Manager Devices & Groups (Devices, Device Groups)
FortiView FortiView & Monitors (Settings, Est. browse time)
Log View Logs (Log stats, Log fields), Log Browse (Log files), Log Groups (no API)
Fabric View Asset Identity Center (Assets, Identities), Subnets (no API)
Incidents & Events Incidents, Event Monitor (Alerts, Alert logs), Event Handlers (no API), Automation (no API), SIEM Log Parsers (no API), FortiGuard Services (Services, Public network, Server access)
FortiAI FortiAI Assistant (no API)
Reports Generated Reports (last 30 days), Report Definitions (All Reports, Chart Library, Macro Library, Datasets), Advanced (Schedules, Languages, Output profiles)
System Settings Logging Topology (no API), Network, Administrative Domains, Fabric Management, Certificates, Log Forwarding, Log Fetching, Event Log (no API), Task Monitor, Mail Server, Syslog Server, Meta Fields, Device Logs, Admin, High Availability, Storage Info, Miscellaneous Settings

The rest of the FortiAnalyzer sidebar#

Entries marked greyed are drawn without a link; hover them for the reason. See Navigation.

Section Entries Who sees it
‹ Global Back to the Global ADOM Everyone
Device The selected FortiAnalyzer, or Select a device Everyone
Operations Calendar, Architecture, Service Diagram, Monitoring (Fleet health → Device health, Metrics, Analysis, Deep monitors, Service Monitor, Analytics, Reports), Search, DNS Lookup, Troubleshooting (Scout, Diagnose Log Collection), Jobs, Device Backups, Import Backup — both greyed Calendar needs users.manage; Scout (the AI assistant) needs advisor.use; Diagnose Log Collection needs write access. Automation Upgrade Flow (greyed), Migration Report (greyed), Automations, Device Provisioning, System Provisioning (greyed), Change Requests, API › Registry & console, Schema builds, Build compatibility The group needs a key that grants configuration writes; Upgrade Flow and Migration Report also need backups.create or backups.restore; Change Requests needs users.manage. In API, Registry & console and Schema builds need registry.view, Build compatibility registry.edit; a profile without write access keeps API as its own group
Administrator Audit Log, Capacity Limits (greyed), Diagnostic Battery, Collection, Change Types, Stored Assets, Device Console, Process, API Tokens, Users, Database, System Automations, Python Studio, Firmware (live by default), Naming, Network Segments, Signatures (greyed), Template Library (greyed), Appliances users.manage; Audit Log also needs audit.view; Python Studio needs studio.script_library or studio.python_console
Plugins Custom Views, Plugin Studio, Lua Studio (greyed) Plugin Studio needs studio.plugin_studio; Lua Studio needs studio.lua_studio
Bottom Users (read-only list), Settings Users: holders of users.view without users.manage; Settings: everyone

Requirements#

  • An appliance registered with kind fortianalyzer under Appliances, with credentials SATOM can use for the JSON-RPC login.
  • A selected FortiAnalyzer (automatic when the ADOM holds exactly one).

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the dashboard and section pages The legacy view gate, which any read permission grants (for example network.view)
Open the measured pages of the FortiAnalyzer menu protection.view
Apply a change on a measured page Any key that grants configuration writes (legacy config_write), for example network.edit or appliances.edit
Create New, Edit, Delete, Preview request, Apply to device Any key that grants configuration writes, for example network.edit or network.apply
Device Manager Authorize / Delete Same as above
Settings → ADOM Menus users.manage
Administrator group users.manage
API → Registry & console (sidebar entry and page, see Product API pages) registry.view

Without write permission, tables show no Actions column, no Create New and no Edit buttons; direct calls to the write endpoints return HTTP 403. On a measured page the dialog shows OK (Read-only: nothing is sent to the device.) instead of saving.

How to use#

Select a FortiAnalyzer#

  1. Choose FortiAnalyzer in the product selector or under ADOMs in the Global sidebar.
  2. Under FortiAnalyzer devices, click Select on the unit.

Browse the measured pages#

  1. With a FortiAnalyzer selected, open the FortiAnalyzer group in the sidebar and click a page, or All pages for the full list in the device's menu order.
  2. A configuration page lists the rows read live from the unit. A monitor or device-managed page says so; click Open it on the device to open the same page in the unit's own GUI in a new tab.

Change a configuration object#

  1. Open the page (for example System Settings → Administrators, or a page of the Not in GUI, but in CLI group) and open the object, or click Create New, or select a row and click Delete.
  2. Change the fields and click Save. SATOM shows Review the change: the exact JSON-RPC request it would send. Nothing has been sent yet.
  3. Click Apply to <device>. SATOM sends the request, reads the object back and shows Verified on the device, Not applied or Not verified.

Read a section#

  1. Open a group in the sidebar and click a section, for example System Settings → Task Monitor.
  2. The title shows on <device> with a LIVE badge. Click a tab to read another endpoint of the same section.
  3. Filter with Search…. The toolbar shows the row count (with + when the list was cut at 500) and the JSON-RPC URL that was read.
  4. Click Refresh to read again.

Edit a configuration table#

  1. Open a writable table, for example System Settings → Syslog Server.
  2. Click the pencil on a row (or Create New, or Edit on a Setting / Value card).
  3. Change the fields in the dialog and click Preview request. The dialog shows the JSON-RPC method, URL and data — Dry-run first — nothing is written until you apply.
  4. Click Apply to device. The page reloads with the new values.

To delete a row, click its trash button. The dialog warns This deletes <name> from the device. Preview the request first. Click Preview request, then Apply to device.

Open a pane that has no API#

  1. Click a section such as Incidents & Events → Event Handlers.
  2. Click Open in FortiAnalyzer to open the unit's own GUI in a new tab, or API & Registry to check whether an endpoint can be bound.

Hide monitor and device-managed pages for everyone#

  1. Open Settings → User Interface → ADOM Menus.
  2. Switch on Hide live-monitor pages (57 pages) and/or Hide pages managed on the device (28 pages).
  3. Click Save. The flash reads ADOM menu settings saved.

The pages leave the menu and the All pages list for every user (on {device} the menu goes from 139 pages to 82, 111 or 54); a direct link still opens them. The configuration harvest is not affected.

Configuration#

What the section pages may write:

Rule Detail
Writable families URLs under /cli/, /dvmdb/ and /report/adom/root/config/
Always read-only Devices, system status, HA status, storage info, tasks, log stats/fields/files, alerts, alert logs, incidents, UEBA assets and identities, generated reports, OFTP certificates
Edit only (no Create New) Network interfaces; local, CA, CRL and remote certificates
No Delete Network interfaces
Row identity name by default; userid for administrators, profileid for admin profiles, seq_num for routes, fieldname for meta fields, layout-id for report layouts, id for several tables

Only scalar fields are sent. Lists, nested objects and device-internal keys (obj flags, oid, obj_ver, dev_ver, keys starting with _) are never written.

Example#

🧪Example — Add a syslog destination

  1. Select faz-01, open System Settings → Syslog Server.
  2. Click Create New, enter the name siem-01 and the server fields.
  3. Preview request shows method add on the syslog URL with the data.
  4. Apply to device. The row appears after the reload, and the Audit Log records faz.create.

Result#

  • Applied writes are audited as faz.create, faz.update or faz.delete with the endpoint, the row key and the changed field names.
  • Previews are not audited and send nothing to the unit.
  • SATOM logs out of the JSON-RPC session after each page read and each write.

Troubleshooting#

"No FortiAnalyzer selected — sections are read live from a device."#

Possible causes — no device selected, or none registered.

Solution — click Pick one on the FortiAnalyzer dashboard; if none is listed, register the unit with kind fortianalyzer.

Verification — the section title shows on <device> and LIVE.

"Device error: login refused (code …)"#

Possible causes — wrong username or password on the appliance record, or the account has no JSON-RPC access on the unit.

Solution — correct the credentials under Administrator → Appliances (or Operations → Appliances) and check the administrator's API access on the FortiAnalyzer.

Verification — the tab lists rows after Refresh.

"Device error: device code …" or "code …: …"#

Possible causes — the unit refused the request, for example because the URL moved on a firmware upgrade or the account lacks rights for it.

Solution — check the endpoint in the FortiAnalyzer API catalog and correct its URL (see Product API pages).

Verification — the tab loads without the red banner.

"endpoint not writable", "create not supported here" or "delete not supported here"#

Possible causes — the table is outside the writable families or on the read-only, no-create or no-delete lists above.

Solution — make the change in the FortiAnalyzer GUI, or with an explicit call in the API console if you hold registry.execute_write.

Verification — not applicable; the restriction is by design.

"Showing the first 500 rows."#

Possible causes — the list has more than 500 entries.

Solution — use the API console with a filter in data, or the unit GUI.

Verification — the row count no longer shows +.

A monitor or device-managed page is missing from the menu#

Possible causes — Settings → ADOM Menus → Hide live-monitor pages or Hide pages managed on the device is on.

Solution — switch it off, or open the page from a direct link.

Verification — the entry reappears in the sidebar.

Advanced#

Advanced Reads, envelopes and limits
  • Each section page builds one FortiAnalyzerClient with a 20-second timeout, logs in, reads the selected tab and logs out.
  • The client chooses between the legacy JSON-RPC envelope and the apiver-3 envelope from the URL family (/logview, /eventmgmt, /incidentmgmt, /report, /fortiview, /fazsys, /ueba, /soarmgmt use apiver 3).
  • Generated Reports adds state=generated and a 30-day time range to the request, because the unit refuses the call without them.
  • A one-row result from anything except a dvmdb_ endpoint is shown as a Setting / Value card.
Advanced ADOM scoping and menu storage
  • Entering any /faz/ or /faz/api/ page switches the browser tab to the FortiAnalyzer ADOM; pages outside the FortiAnalyzer allow-list redirect to /faz/.
  • The hidden-menu list is stored as the faz.hidden_menu application setting and replicated like other settings. Unknown keys are dropped.
  • Firmware in the Administrator group opens the shared firmware library scoped to FortiAnalyzer images (see Firmware).
